To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in benign melanocytic tumour cells proliferation is negligible and motility is high, whereas in malignant tumours motility is negligible and proliferation is high.
in melanocytic skin nevi, proliferation and motility of tumour cells are in balance, whereas in malignant skin melanomas, proliferation clearly dominates motility.
the relative probability of motility is significantly higher than the probability of proliferation in benign common nevs, whereas the reverse is true for malignant melanocytic skin tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach for the quantitative analysis of tumour morphology.
a novel approach to estimate tumour cell proliferation from tumour morphology.
the development of a new method for the quantitative analysis of the relative probabilities for motility and proliferation in human tumours.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in benign melanocytic nevi tumour growth is mainly due to cell migration, whereas in malignant nevi tumour cell proliferation is the major driving force.
tumour cell proliferation, but not motility, is an essential prerequisite of malignant tumour growth.
the morphological patterns of benign common nevi and malignant melanoma are determined by the relative probabilities of proliferation and motile behaviour of the respective tumour cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in malignant melanoma the tumour cells are not only proliferating, but are also migrating.
the relative probabilities of proliferation and motile behaviour of individual tumour cells can be estimated from tumour morphology.
tumour cell proliferation is the major factor for invasive tumour cell growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphological analysis of tumour patterns in histological slides of human tumours may be a useful tool to assess the biological aggressiveness of human tumours.
tumour cell motile behaviour is an important factor in the formation of benign common nevi and that tumour cell proliferation plays a dominant role in malignant melanocytomas.
the morphological patterns of tumour cells can be used to estimate the relative importance of proliferation and motile behaviour.
